best_architecture: Layered 'parse once, query many' AST service with a polyglot core and language-specific edit backends, serving two roles for Local-Claw: (A) context manager that builds a ranked repo map feeding the Gemma 4 brain, and (B) structural editor enabling safe refactors beyond line-based edits. (1) PARSING LAYER — tree-sitter as the universal parser. It produces a concrete syntax tree per file, is error-tolerant (returns a usable tree even on syntactically broken / in-progress code, where LSP and Semgrep fail), supports incremental re-parsing of only the edited region (~36x faster in reported benchmarks), and has uniform grammars + an S-expression query language across Python/TypeScript/Rust/Go. One parser, one query dialect, all languages — the agent never depends on the LLM to 'read' structure. (2) SYMBOL-MAP LAYER — run tree-sitter tag/scope queries (the standard tags.scm / locals.scm shipped per grammar) to extract definitions (functions, classes, methods, structs, traits) and references (calls, type uses, imports). Build a directed symbol/file graph where edges point from each reference site to its definition (Aider 'repo map' pattern). Rank symbols with personalized PageRank over the graph (networkx) — bias toward files in the agent's active working set (Aider uses ~50x multiplier for chat-referenced files) — then pack top-ranked signatures into an adaptive token budget and emit as structured JSONL (name, kind, signature, parent, file:line) so it is both LLM-readable and machine-queryable. Cache parsed trees keyed by file mtime/hash for incremental updates. (3) STRUCTURAL SEARCH/EDIT LAYER — split read-only matching from semantic rewrites. For polyglot structural search-and-replace, use ast-grep (Rust, multi-core, library + CLI, meta-variables $VAR / $$$MULTI + YAML rules). For genuinely SEMANTIC TypeScript/JavaScript refactors that must follow the type system (rename a symbol and update every cross-file reference, move a symbol between files and fix imports), tree-sitter is NOT enough — use ts-morph (wraps the TS Compiler API, has a real type checker and cross-file reference resolution); edit in-memory then save() atomically. For security/taint, use Semgrep. POLYGLOT STRATEGY: one stable agent-facing interface (get_symbols, find_references, repo_map, search, rewrite, rename) routed per language — tree-sitter for parsing/symbol-map everywhere; ast-grep for syntactic search-rewrite everywhere; ts-morph for type-aware TS/JS edits; rope/jedi (Python) or rust-analyzer (Rust) where true semantic rename is required. KEY DECISIONS: (a) prefer error-tolerant tree-sitter over compiler/LSP for the always-on symbol map so the agent works on broken code mid-edit; (b) separate cheap polyglot structural match (ast-grep) from expensive type-aware semantic refactor (ts-morph/LSP); (c) cache + incrementally update parsed trees; (d) rank-and-budget the symbol map (PageRank + token budget) rather than dumping all symbols; (e) for any rewrite, manipulate the AST and re-print, never text/regex replacement. [uncertain: exact PageRank personalization multiplier is Aider-specific and may need tuning for Local-Claw]

code2seq: Generating Sequences from Structured Representations of Code (Alon, Brody, Levy, Yahav 2019) - arxiv:1808.01400 - ICLR'19 - encodes compositional AST paths with BiLSTM + attention; basis for AST-aware code summarization/retrieval

RepoGraph: Enhancing AI Software Engineering with Repository-level Code Graph (Ouyang et al. 2024) - arxiv:2410.14684 - builds a repository-level code graph (definitions/references/calls) to give agents holistic cross-file structure for SWE-bench-style tasks

CodexGraph: Bridging Large Language Models and Code Repositories via Code Graph Databases (Liu et al. 2024) - arxiv:2408.03910 - indexes a repo into a graph DB and lets LLM agents query structure (classes-under-module, method-to-definition) precisely; evaluated on CrossCodeEval, SWE-bench, EvoCodeBench

LocAgent: Graph-Guided LLM Agents for Code Localization (Chen et al. 2025) - arxiv:2503.09089 - graph-guided traversal over code structure for code localization, modeling directory/file hierarchy and symbol relations
RANGER: Repository-Level Agent for Graph-Enhanced Retrieval (2025) - arxiv:2509.25257 - graph-centric retrieval encoding definitions/references/calls for repository-level agent reasoning

cAST: Enhancing Code Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Structural Chunking via Abstract Syntax Tree (Zhang et al. 2025) - arxiv:2506.15655 - parses code into an AST and greedily merges AST nodes into syntax-aware chunks instead of fixed line-based chunking; directly relevant to AST-aware code context

pitfalls: Using tree-sitter for TypeScript semantic refactors. Tree-sitter sees syntax, not types — a rename via tree-sitter misses cross-file reference resolution and will rename unrelated identifiers that happen to share a name. Use ts-morph (real type checker, findReferencesAsNodes) for any cross-file TS/JS rename or move-symbol; reserve tree-sitter for parsing and the symbol map.

Re-parsing on every agent call. Not caching parsed trees keyed by file mtime/content-hash makes parsing O(N x calls) for large repos and defeats tree-sitter's incremental advantage. Maintain a cache (file path -> {mtime/hash, tree, tags}) and only reparse changed files.

Text/regex replacement instead of AST-print. Regex replaces inside string literals and comments and corrupts code structure. Always manipulate the AST (ast-grep rewrite or ts-morph) and re-print; run dry-run/preview before saving.

Grammar/binding version mismatch. py-tree-sitter and a grammar package built against a different C ABI cause ImportError or, worse, silent tree corruption. Pin py-tree-sitter and grammar versions together (prefer tree-sitter-language-pack for a coherent pre-built set) and verify ABI compatibility at install time.

PageRank tuned to a non-default multiplier without empirical validation. Applying the ~50x personalization boost to ALL files equally (or copying Aider's constant blindly) defeats the personalization that makes the repo map useful — only the active/chat files should be boosted, and the multiplier should be validated against retrieval quality for Local-Claw's repos.

JSONL symbol map growing unbounded for mono-repos. 100k symbols x ~100 tokens each overflows the Gemma context window. Hard-cap output at the configured token budget and use importance ranking strictly as a filter — emit ranked definitions until the budget is hit, then truncate with an ellipsis marker.

ast-grep pattern too broad. A pattern like `foo($A)` matches unintended functions named foo across namespaces. Scope patterns with metavariable constraints, language-specific node kinds, or YAML rule conditions (inside/has/kind) so the codemod is surgical.

Semgrep taint propagation on a large codebase. Semgrep taint analysis can be O(N^2) for some patterns and take minutes on mono-repos; free cross-function/inter-file taint also moved behind the paid platform in Jan 2025. Reserve Semgrep for targeted security rules, not everyday agent refactors, and prefer ast-grep for general structural work.

Treating ast-grep / tree-sitter as semantic tools generally. Neither does type inference, scope resolution, or call-graph resolution. If a spec promises 'find all references' or 'rename safely across files' using ast-grep alone, it is wrong — route those to ts-morph (TS) or a language server (Python/Rust).

ts-morph misconfiguration. Pass an absolute tsConfigFilePath (relative paths are misinterpreted) and remember edits stay in memory until save() — forgetting to save, or skipping the dry-run preview, leads to lost or unintended edits.
bdd_gherkin_scenarios:
Feature: AST-based repo map and structural editing for Local-Claw

  Background:
    Given a multi-language repository parsed with tree-sitter
    And parsed trees are cached keyed by file mtime/content-hash
    And the repo map is emitted as JSONL with fields name, kind, signature, parent, file:line

  Scenario: Token-budgeted repo map ranked by importance
    Given a Python repository containing 500 extracted symbols
    And the active working set (chat files) is ["app/service.py"]
    When the repo-map skill is invoked with a 2000-token budget
    Then symbols are ranked by personalized PageRank with chat files boosted
    And only the top-ranked symbols that fit within 2000 tokens are emitted as JSONL
    And no full source file is included verbatim
    And lower-ranked symbols are dropped rather than overflowing the budget

  Scenario: Tree-sitter error tolerance on broken code
    Given a TypeScript file containing a syntax error mid-edit
    When the parsing layer parses the file
    Then tree-sitter returns a partial concrete syntax tree containing an ERROR node
    And no exception is raised
    And the symbols outside the error region are still extracted into the map

  Scenario: Cross-file TypeScript rename via ts-morph
    Given a function "computeTotal" referenced across 5 TypeScript files
    When the structural editor renames it to "computeOrderTotal" using ts-morph
    Then all 5 files are updated using the type checker's reference resolution
    And import statements referencing the symbol are corrected
    And an identically named local symbol in an unrelated scope is NOT renamed
    And changes are previewed in memory before save() is called

  Scenario: Polyglot structural search with ast-grep
    Given a Python codebase that makes HTTP calls
    When the agent searches for the pattern "requests.get($URL)"
    Then all HTTP GET call sites are found regardless of the variable bound to $URL
    And matches inside string literals and comments are NOT returned
    And each match reports its file and line for the agent to act on
sota_improvements: Code graph DB beyond PageRank (CodexGraph arxiv:2408.03910 / RepoGraph arxiv:2410.14684): index the full repo into a graph (NetworkX or Neo4j) of definitions/references/calls so the agent can run multi-hop 'what calls what calls what' queries that a flat PageRank ranking cannot answer — enables precise code localization for SWE tasks.

LSP-as-a-service: run rust-analyzer / pylsp (and tsserver) as persistent language servers and query hover/definition/references over the LSP protocol for true semantic refactors across all languages, not just TS — gives Python and Rust the same cross-file correctness ts-morph gives TypeScript.

ast-grep programmatic library API instead of subprocess: use ast-grep-py (PyPI, native bindings, released 2026) or the Rust ast-grep-core crate to embed structural search/rewrite in-process, avoiding per-call subprocess startup cost and enabling richer match inspection.

AST-aware structural chunking (cAST, arxiv:2506.15655) for any RAG/embedding step: greedily merge AST nodes into syntax-aware chunks rather than fixed line windows so functions/classes stay intact, improving retrieval quality of the repo context fed to Gemma.

tree-sitter WASM grammars: compile grammars to WASM so the same parsing/symbol-map logic can run in a browser/Electron skill UI without native binary deps — useful for a future web-based Local-Claw front end.

Expose ast-grep as discrete MCP-style tools (dump_syntax_tree / find_code / find_code_by_rule / test_match_code_rule, per ast-grep/ast-grep-mcp) so the agent authors, verifies, and iteratively improves codemod rules instead of guessing one-shot rewrites.
Rebuild the personalized-PageRank token-budgeted repo map before each LLM call (Aider pattern) so context adapts to the evolving working set, rather than serving a static, stale map.
